    Masaaki Sytrenis¶

    "I didn't stop the mountain. I made it listen."

    Masaaki Sytrenis — called "Sytrenis the Diplomat" — was a catmen hero of the Human Age, born in 1667 BGD. He is the founder of the ancient catmen religion Sytrenis, and, more than any other figure, the reason the catmen of Ge'or exist as a people rather than a memory: he ended the persecution that nearly exterminated them. The The Great Epic of the Heroes of Donblond'werv records his deeds.

    The Party¶

    Sytrenis was part of an adventurer group whose names live on in the epic:

    • Hogryr Aledini — a catmen companion
    • Trurdrang Emberflare — a kobold companion
    • Laudlaern Kenismov — a human companion

    They met when the three saved Sytrenis's life: a local human had beaten him and left him clutching a twig on the edge of a mountain, and it was Kenismov who reached out and pulled him back. Sytrenis trained his skills hard and eventually became the party's main diplomat.

    The Kingdom of Termopolas¶

    The party first won their fame saving the kingdom of Termopolas — a heavily xenophobic empire in the region that is now the Erisian Empire, which was exterminating catmen. The persecution bred the Lesser Catmen themselves: driven to starvation in the chaos, some catmen were forever changed — smaller, lighter, a new breed shaped by hunger. In the region of the now-Munchon, a great mountain rose over the land — a mountain that was never a mountain.

    The Metrak Incident¶

    In ~1645 BGD — at twenty-two years old — after a catmen girl, Sithia, abandoned him, Sytrenis walked alone toward the mountain Metrak while his party slept. His companions hunted for him for weeks and found him paralyzed at the dungeon's mouth; he convinced them to enter.

    Inside, past ancient scriptures in a long-lost language, the mountain's old systems tried to kill them. They fled, and over months and other dungeons pieced together the terrifying truth: the "mountain" was a monster capable of destroying a continent.

    Emperor Atanides of Termopolas — "the Archaeologer" — had already sent a thousand men into the Metrak dungeon, with him and a hundred more waiting at the door. The machine woke. It killed Atanides and raged across the land to the frontier of the now-Grimmel Republic, leaving no city behind.

    Sytrenis raised two hundred men and marched. Most died. With a rope and a spear he reached the dungeon entrance, found the dead, and found a green rune-like symbol on the door and a strange suit (a nuclear symbol; a protection suit). He wore the suit, the turrets fell silent, and a button stood shining. He pressed it — and the machine stopped. A great map shone in the air, showing sixteen regions of Erisdar with sixteen identical machines — the Metraks, city-sized robots of the Last Great War. A printer ran and ran, spitting maps.

    Sytrenis the Diplomat¶

    Termopolas, now without an emperor, branded Sytrenis and his party criminals and blamed them for the tragedy — but the Tunwif kingdom, along with Aelefer and Lima, shielded them, starting the Tunwif–Termopolas conflict. Termopolas, leaderless and broken in morale, lost battle after battle despite a three-to-one advantage, and finally gave up the hunt.

    Sytrenis then gave peace a chance: he explained that he had saved the entire continent from being ravaged by the Metrak, and made peace between the kingdom of Tunwif and Termopolas. He earned his title — "Sytrenis the Diplomat" — and with it, the persecution of catmen ended across the continent.

    The Lesser Catmen's Ancestor¶

    The Lesser Catmen revere Sytrenis as their ancestor and try to follow his path — to be diplomats. His faith, Sytrenis, endures as the ancient religion of the catmen.
